Add Breedbase plot names to a design

Source: R/breedbase_brapi.R
add_plot_names.Rd

Adds a plot_name column to design$design with the names the plots will have in Breedbase, so they can be seen, checked with breedbase_check() and changed before save_breedbase(). The design functions call this when given a trial_name. Run it again to make the names for another trial name or pattern, or edit the column by hand: any unique names are accepted. save_breedbase(), phenotype_template() and first_stage_values() use the stored names.

Usage

add_plot_names(
  design,
  trial_name = NULL,
  location = NULL,
  plot_name_pattern = "{trial}_{location}_{accession}_{block}_{rep}",
  plot_names = NULL
)

Arguments

design

A design from augmented_row_column_design(), augmented_prep_design(), resolvable_row_column_design(), as_breedbase_design() or prepare_breedbase_trial().

trial_name

The Breedbase trial name. For a multi-location p-rep design, the location is added as in save_breedbase() (one trial per location). Can be omitted for a prepared Breedbase trial.

location

The Breedbase location of the trial, used by the {location} field of the pattern. Not needed for p-rep designs (their own locations are used, or give a named vector mapping them to Breedbase locations, as in save_breedbase()) or for a prepared Breedbase trial (its recorded location is used).

plot_name_pattern

Pattern for the names, as in save_breedbase(): fields {trial}, {location}, {accession}, {block}, {rep}, {plot}, {row} and {col}.

plot_names

Optional names given by you instead of a pattern: one per row of design$design, or the name of a column holding them.

Value

The design with a plot_name column (NA for filler plots, which are not saved) and the trial name in plot_name_trial.

Examples

rc <- augmented_row_column_design(paste0("G", 1:108), paste0("C", 1:4),
                                  12, 12, 4, 4, n_candidates = 5, seed = 1)
rc <- add_plot_names(rc, "AYT_2026", location = "Ibadan")
head(rc$design$plot_name)
#> [1] "AYT_2026_Ibadan_G31_1_1"  "AYT_2026_Ibadan_G70_1_1" 
#> [3] "AYT_2026_Ibadan_G104_1_1" "AYT_2026_Ibadan_C4_1_1"  
#> [5] "AYT_2026_Ibadan_G66_2_1"  "AYT_2026_Ibadan_G5_2_1"  
# Other names, e.g. with the field position:
rc <- add_plot_names(rc, "AYT_2026_Ibadan", plot_name_pattern = "{trial}_{plot}_r{row}c{col}")
head(rc$design$plot_name)
#> [1] "AYT_2026_Ibadan_1_r1c1" "AYT_2026_Ibadan_2_r1c2" "AYT_2026_Ibadan_3_r1c3"
#> [4] "AYT_2026_Ibadan_4_r1c4" "AYT_2026_Ibadan_5_r1c5" "AYT_2026_Ibadan_6_r1c6"
